name: cap:actor-runners
description: Running an actor through a runner process: launch, limits, cancel, and one trusted outcome

name: cap:actors
description: Who holds a role: an agent or a person, and how each is defined in config

name: cap:artifact-store
description: Content-addressed store for large or sensitive run artifacts, such as transcripts, kept by hash

name: cap:claude-code-runner
description: Running an actor through Claude Code, mapping its stream-json onto run events

name: cap:cli
description: The troupe command line: a thin client over the core, with its flags, output and exit codes

name: cap:client-protocol
description: Commands and queries every surface uses to reach the core, as JSON Schema messages

name: cap:collaboration
description: Working across installs and machines: approvals and answers that travel between people

name: cap:config
description: A theatre's config as events with lineage, merged across branches, and the actor, its first kind

name: cap:config-files
description: Config projected to files under .troupe/ for review as diffs, never losing a file a person wrote

name: cap:core-api
description: The core's commands and queries, which the CLI, run server and UIs all call

name: cap:cues
description: Open requests addressed to a role, with a brief, raised by gates and escalations

name: cap:development
description: How troupe itself is built, tested and released: the check, flaky tests, Python versions, releases

name: cap:docs-publishing
description: How a change to troupe reaches troupe.run: which pushes rebuild /docs, what the notice job may do

name: cap:effects
description: What an actor may touch (files, network), declared in config and enforced by its stage

name: cap:escalation
description: How an agent gets a decision: research first, then a brief to the role that owns it

name: cap:event-store
description: Append-only text events git can merge, read back in a stable order across branches and forks

name: cap:flake-hunt
description: Finding flaky tests on demand, on every platform: repeated rounds, load, fresh inputs, evidence

name: cap:flows
description: How actors are arranged: in sequence, in parallel with fork and join, in loops, and as swarms

name: cap:gates
description: Points where work waits for a decision from the role that owns it

name: cap:guests
description: Installable packs that add to troupe, with their own config files and schemas

name: cap:house
description: The long-lived local process that serves theatres and keeps projections live

name: cap:identity
description: Working out who is acting through a chain of sources, and refusing when nobody can be named

name: cap:infrastructure
description: The troupe-run org's own setup, not a troupe capability

name: cap:lifecycle
description: TBD

name: cap:lineage
description: What every event records about itself: who, through what, when, why, change, cause, approvals

name: cap:notes
description: What a performance teaches, recorded and fed into the next one

name: cap:notifications
description: Telling a role's holder that something needs them, through pluggable channels

name: cap:performance
description: One run of a process: starting, following and ending a performance

name: cap:platform
description: The one seam for OS-specific behaviour: files, locks, processes, interrupts, file watching, paths

name: cap:plugins
description: Ports, transports (direct or JSON-RPC), and how plugins are declared, acquired and trusted

name: cap:policy
description: Authoritative settings read through one seam; a lower level can tighten, never loosen

name: cap:projections
description: Read models folded from events, such as config files, run status and logs

name: cap:protocol
description: Strict, language-neutral JSON Schema contracts in protocol/ and each plugin, for every surface

name: cap:python-support
description: Which Python versions troupe supports, how that is declared and enforced, in step with CI

name: cap:quality-check
description: What scripts/check.py runs, its scoped form, and which paths need which part of the check

name: cap:releases
description: Versions, changelogs and releases, derived from Conventional Commits through a release PR

name: cap:roles
description: Jobs in a process, such as reviewer; who holds each, and routing work to roles

name: cap:run-workspaces
description: Where a run works, in its own git worktree, and how its changes are seen, accepted or discarded

name: cap:runner-protocol
description: The JSON-RPC contract between troupe and a runner, so runners can be written in any language

name: cap:runs
description: Recording each run of an actor with lineage, and reading runs back: status, logs, follow

name: cap:scripted-runner
description: The deterministic test runner that plays scripts or replays recorded streams

name: cap:settings
description: Named settings with one default each, and how project, user and house levels layer

name: cap:stages
description: Where an actor runs, and whether its effects can be enforced there: local, Docker, others

name: cap:storage
description: Where troupe keeps state and caches on disk, per theatre and per user

name: cap:telemetry
description: Anonymous usage data: asked for, recorded as an event, inspectable, off when nobody can be asked

name: cap:theatre
description: A project troupe serves: a directory with troupe config, addressed by id

name: cap:user-docs
description: troupe's user docs, built into troupe.run's /docs: page contract, generated reference, vocabulary

name: cap:vcs
description: The version-control port: git or a plain filesystem, read for lineage and the event store

name: cap:work-tracking
description: Reading and updating tracked work (issues, epics, labels) through a tracker port
